English Skills Challenge

Imagine your friend is planning a city break. Explore two destinations, understand travel information and make a recommendation. Complete the individual challenges first; the speaking cards are for the final pair activity.

📖 Reading🎧 Listening✍️ Writing🗣️ Speaking – later
Complete Reading, Listening and Writing before submitting
Skill 01 · Read and explore

Two Cities, Two Experiences

Your friend has two possible destinations for a short holiday. Read the descriptions and answer the questions. Choose the best answer (A, B or C).

DESTINATION A

Lisbon, Portugal

Lisbon is a sunny coastal city known for its colourful buildings, historic neighbourhoods and beautiful viewpoints. Visitors can explore the narrow streets of Alfama, ride the famous yellow trams and enjoy fresh seafood in small local restaurants. The city is built on several hills, so comfortable shoes are a good idea. Many attractions are close to one another, but walking uphill can be tiring. Spring and early autumn are pleasant times to visit because the weather is usually warm without the busiest summer crowds.

DESTINATION B

Amsterdam, Netherlands

Amsterdam is famous for its canals, bicycles and world-class museums. Visitors can take a boat tour, cycle along quiet streets or spend an afternoon at the Rijksmuseum. The city is relatively compact, and public transport makes it easy to move between different areas. Amsterdam can be rainy and windy, even in summer, so packing a light waterproof jacket is useful. The city attracts many tourists throughout the year. Booking popular museums in advance can help visitors avoid long queues.

Reading tip: First, identify key words in the question. Then scan the text for the same idea, not necessarily the exact same words. For inference questions, combine clues from the text with logical thinking.

1. Which city is especially associated with cycling and canals?

2. Why might spring or early autumn be a good time to visit Lisbon?

3. A traveller has difficulty walking long distances uphill. Which destination may be more convenient, according to the texts?

4. What can be inferred about visiting a popular museum in Amsterdam?

5. Which statement best compares the two destinations?

Reading · Answers and feedback
  1. B – Amsterdam. It is known for its canals and bicycles.
  2. A. The text says the weather is pleasant and crowds may be smaller than in summer.
  3. B – Amsterdam. Lisbon has several hills and walking uphill can be tiring; Amsterdam is compact and has public transport.
  4. B. Booking in advance helps avoid long queues.
  5. A. Both have cultural attractions, but Lisbon is associated with historic neighbourhoods and trams, while Amsterdam is associated with canals, cycling and museums.

Skill 03 · Write to recommend

Help Your Friend Choose!

Your friend is choosing between Lisbon and Amsterdam for a short holiday. Write a message of 80–100 words recommending one city.

Include: mention both cities; compare at least two characteristics (activities, attractions, food or atmosphere); recommend one city; explain why; and give one practical suggestion.

Useful language

Comparing

Lisbon is more… than…
Amsterdam is famous for…, while…
Both cities have…

Recommending

I'd recommend visiting…
You should definitely…
You could also…
…because…

Your message

0 words · Aim for 80–100 words

Self-check before you finish

Use this checklist to review your message. You do not need to tick every box to submit.

Writing · Sample answer for comparison

Hi Alex! I know you're choosing between Lisbon and Amsterdam. Both cities are beautiful, but they offer different experiences. Lisbon is famous for its colourful streets, historic neighbourhoods and sunny weather, while Amsterdam is known for its canals, bicycles and museums. I'd recommend visiting Amsterdam because it is compact and easy to explore by public transport or bike. You should visit the Rijksmuseum and take a canal tour. Remember to pack a waterproof jacket because the weather can be rainy!

Note: Other recommendations are valid if they are clear and supported with relevant details.

Skill 04 · Pair conversation · Do this after the individual tasks

Travel Talk: Speaking Cards

Work with a partner in your breakout room. Choose 3–4 cards. Take turns answering and asking follow-up questions. Try to extend your answers with reasons and examples.

• Which country would you love to visit?

• Do you prefer a beach holiday or a city break?

• What makes a destination special for you?

• Who would you like to travel with?

• What is the most interesting place you have visited?

• Have you ever had an unexpected experience while travelling?

• What was the best thing about that trip?

• Would you recommend it?

• Do you enjoy trying local food when you travel?

• What Colombian dish should tourists try?

• Would you visit a city mainly for its food?

• What cultural experience would you recommend?

• Do you prefer travelling on a budget or in luxury?

• Famous attractions or hidden gems?

• Do you prefer travelling alone or with other people?

• Why?

• You have two days in a new city. What would you do?

• Which places would you visit?

• What food would you try?

• How would you organise your time?

• What would you do if you got lost in a foreign city?

• What advice would you give a first-time traveller?

• How can tourists travel responsibly?

• What is one thing you should never forget?

Useful language for your conversation

Giving opinions

I think… / In my opinion…
I'd rather… / I prefer… because…

Keeping it going

What about you? / Why do you think so?
Have you ever…? / Can you tell me more?
That's interesting!

Remember: Don't give one-word answers. Explain your ideas, ask your partner a follow-up question and react to what they say.
